Source: A 67-year-old man presents to the emergency room reporting sudden-onset abdominal and back pain that began 3 hours ago.
He denies any diarrhea or hematochezia and says the pain is not affected by movement.
Physical exam is notable for diffuse abdominal tenderness without rigidity or guarding.
He has a 45-pack-year smoking history, but he does not drink alcohol or use any illicit drugs.
During evaluation, the patient becomes diaphoretic and pale and reports that he feels fatigued.
He currently takes amlodipine and atorvastatin and is compliant with his medications.
He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and depression.
